title: The Unreliable Narrator
text:
Few devices in fiction have generated as much critical debate as the unreliable narrator, whose account the reader is invited to doubt. In such novels, the narrator's self-justifications gradually betray a distortion of the events being recounted. Readers must therefore reconstruct the truth from the gaps, contradictions, and evasions that the narrator inadvertently reveals. The technique thus transforms the act of reading into a form of detective work.

Critics have debated whether the device is primarily a moral instrument or an aesthetic one. Some argue that it exposes the self-deception that governs ordinary human memory, while others contend that it merely showcases the author's technical ingenuity. Yet both readings converge on a single insight: the text does not simply tell a story, but dramatises the difficulty of telling one honestly. The narrator's failure becomes, paradoxically, the most revealing feature of the work.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must readers do when a narrator is unreliable?
options: Accept every event exactly as the narrator describes it
Reconstruct the truth from gaps and contradictions
Ignore the narrator and read only the dialogue

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do some critics argue about the device?
options: It exposes the self-deception found in ordinary memory
It has no effect on the reader's understanding
It is used only in historical fiction
It makes the story shorter and simpler

questions.text: What can be inferred about the reader's role in a novel with an unreliable narrator?
options: The reader is a passive recipient of the story
The reader becomes an active interpreter of the text
The reader should avoid analysing the narrator
The reader's judgement is irrelevant to the meaning

questions.text: Why does the author describe the narrator's failure as 'paradoxically' revealing?
options: Because the narrator's errors expose the difficulty of honest storytelling
Because the narrator always tells the truth in the end
Because the failure makes the novel less interesting
Because critics have rejected the device entirely

a change that makes something untrue or misrepresented
avoidances of giving a direct or honest answer
presents something in a vivid or emotional way

paragraph_translations: Poucos recursos da ficção geraram tanto debate crítico quanto o narrador não confiável, cujo relato o leitor é convidado a duvidar. Nesses romances, as autojustificativas do narrador revelam, aos poucos, uma distorção dos eventos que ele mesmo narra. Assim, o leitor precisa reconstruir a verdade a partir das lacunas, contradições e evasivas que o narrador revela sem querer. A técnica transforma, portanto, o ato de ler em uma forma de trabalho de detetive.

Os críticos têm debatido se o recurso é, sobretudo, um instrumento moral ou estético. Alguns argumentam que ele expõe a autoilusão que governa a memória humana comum, enquanto outros sustentam que ele apenas exibe a engenhosidade técnica do autor. Ainda assim, ambas as leituras convergem em um mesmo entendimento: o texto não apenas conta uma história, mas dramatiza a dificuldade de contá-la com honestidade. O fracasso do narrador torna-se, paradoxalmente, o aspecto mais revelador da obra.
